title: Seoul Weather This Week and What to Wear: Late October 2026 Outfit Guide for Travelers
html:
Heading to Seoul in late October? You've picked one of the best times of the year to visit. The air is dry and clear, the trees are turning yellow and red, and the days are pleasant for walking. But there's one thing that surprises many first-time visitors: the temperature changes a lot in a single day. A warm, sunny afternoon can turn into a chilly evening very quickly.

This guide looks at Seoul's real weather this week (checked on the morning of Friday, October 23, 2026) and tells you exactly what to wear — plus what Koreans themselves do to stay comfortable in autumn.

Seoul Weather Right Now (October 23, 2026)

Here's what it looks like in Seoul this morning:

  • Right now (around 11:45 a.m.): 15°C (59°F), mostly clear skies, light wind. It feels like about 15°C.
  • Today's range: a cold 7°C (45°F) early in the morning, up to about 19°C (66°F) in the afternoon.
  • Humidity: around 64% — comfortable, not sticky like summer.
  • Rain: very little chance today.

In short: it's classic Seoul autumn weather. Sunny, fresh, and perfect for palaces, parks, and long walks — as long as you dress for both the cool morning and the warm afternoon.

Yellow ginkgo trees in Olympic Park, Seoul — a typical autumn view. Photo: Firadrn, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

The Big Surprise: A 12°C Gap Between Morning and Afternoon

Today, the difference between the coldest and warmest time of day is about 12°C (22°F). That's normal for Seoul in autumn. The sky is clear, so the sun warms the city quickly in the day, but the heat escapes fast after sunset.

What this means for you:

  • Early morning (before 9 a.m.): it can feel like early winter. You'll want a jacket.
  • Afternoon (12–4 p.m.): it can feel almost like late spring. A long-sleeve shirt alone may be enough in the sun.
  • Evening (after sunset, around 5:45 p.m. these days): it gets cool again fast — especially on high places like Namsan (N Seoul Tower) or by the Han River, where it's also windy.

So if you plan a full day out — palace in the morning, café in the afternoon, night view in the evening — you'll go through all three "seasons" in one day.

Seoul at dusk, seen from Namsan. Evening views like this are beautiful, but it gets chilly up here after sunset. Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

What to Wear This Week: The Layering Method

The easiest way to deal with big temperature changes is layering. This simply means wearing a few thin pieces of clothing on top of each other, instead of one thick piece. When it gets warm, you take a layer off. When it gets cold, you put it back on.

A simple outfit that works for Seoul right now:

  • Base: a T-shirt or thin long-sleeve top.
  • Middle: a light sweater, cardigan, hoodie, or sweatshirt.
  • Outer: a light jacket or trench coat (a denim jacket, light windbreaker, or blazer works too).
  • Bottom: long pants or jeans. Shorts are too cold for the morning and evening.
  • Shoes: comfortable sneakers. You'll walk a lot — Seoul's palaces, markets, and subway transfers add up to 15,000+ steps a day easily. Many neighborhoods (like Bukchon or Namsan) are also hilly.

Tip: bring a small backpack or tote bag. When you take off your jacket in the afternoon, you'll need somewhere to put it.

People in jackets and light coats near Myeongdong Cathedral on a sunny, cool day. Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

This Weekend: Warm and Sunny — Great for Outdoor Plans

The weekend looks even warmer than today:

  • Saturday, Oct 24: about 14–20°C (57–68°F), cloudy at times.
  • Sunday, Oct 25: about 15–23°C (73°F), partly sunny.
  • Monday, Oct 26: about 15–23°C, with a small chance of rain (around 25%).

These are great days for outdoor plans, like a picnic at a Hangang Park (the big riverside parks along the Han River, the river that runs through the middle of Seoul) or an autumn walk around a palace. In the afternoon, a T-shirt with a light top may be all you need. Still, keep a light jacket in your bag for the evening — it'll drop back to around 15°C after dark.

Yeouido Hangang Park on a clear late-autumn day. Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Heads-Up: A Cold Snap Next Tuesday and Wednesday

Here's the important part if you're in Seoul next week. The forecast shows a sudden drop in temperature:

  • Tuesday, Oct 27: about 5–16°C (41–61°F).
  • Wednesday, Oct 28: about 3–11°C (37–52°F) — the coldest day of the week, cloudy.
  • Thursday, Oct 29: about 6–15°C, with some chance of rain (around 35%).

Going from 23°C on Monday to a morning near 3°C on Wednesday is a big jump. A light jacket alone won't be enough. For these days, add:

  • A warm coat (wool coat) or a light padded jacket.
  • A knit sweater under your coat.
  • A scarf if you're out early in the morning or late at night.

Didn't pack for this? No problem. Seoul is one of the easiest cities in the world to buy clothes. Big stores like Uniqlo, SPAO, and Topten are in almost every shopping area (Myeongdong, Hongdae, Gangnam), and Dongdaemun's shopping malls sell cheap jackets and sweaters until late at night.

On colder days, padded jackets come out fast — like at this market food stall in the Dongdaemun area in late November. Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Dress Like a Local: How Koreans Handle Autumn Weather

Koreans take the daily temperature seriously when getting dressed. A few things locals actually do:

  • They check the "outfit by temperature" chart. In Korea, a popular chart called gion-byeol otcharim (기온별 옷차림, "outfits by temperature") is shared everywhere online. People look at the day's high and low and dress by the chart. We've put a simple English version in the table below.
  • They check the weather app every morning. Most Koreans use the Naver Weather (네이버 날씨) or the Korea Meteorological Administration's weather app. Both show hour-by-hour temperatures, so you can see exactly when it will warm up or cool down.
  • They dress for the subway, too. Inside the subway and in big shopping malls, it's warm — sometimes very warm. That's another reason locals wear layers they can open or take off easily, instead of one heavy sweater.
  • They watch the air quality. In spring and late autumn, Seoul sometimes has fine dust (tiny particles in the air, called misemeonji). On "bad" air days, many people wear a KF94 mask, which you can buy at any convenience store or pharmacy.
Commuters on a Seoul subway train in late November — notice the layers and coats. Photo: kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Quick Guide: What to Wear by Temperature

Here's a simple version of the Korean "outfit by temperature" chart. Look up the day's high and low in a weather app, then find the matching rows.

TemperatureWhat to WearThis Week in Seoul
20–23°C (68–73°F)Long-sleeve top or T-shirt + thin cardiganSat–Mon afternoons
17–19°C (63–66°F)Sweatshirt, hoodie, or light knit; light jacketToday's afternoon
12–16°C (54–61°F)Jacket, trench coat, or cardigan + long pantsMost evenings; Tue & Thu afternoons
9–11°C (48–52°F)Trench coat or thick jacket + knit sweaterWed afternoon
5–8°C (41–46°F)Wool coat or light padded jacket, knit, scarfToday's early morning; Tue & Thu mornings
4°C and below (39°F and below)Padded coat, warm inner layer, scarf, glovesWed early morning (about 3°C)

Good to know: the forecast above was checked on October 23, 2026, and forecasts can change — especially for days further away. Check Naver Weather or any weather app the night before, and pick your layers from the table.

meta_description: Seoul weather for late October 2026: big day-night temperature swings and a cold snap ahead. What to wear, layering tips, and a temperature chart.
